newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GLAVERBEL SAYS H2 SHOWING IMPROVEMENT.
newsitem.headline: GLAVERBEL SAYS H2 SHOWING IMPROVEMENT.

text.p: Belgian glassmaker Glaverbel Group said on Thursday that results were showing improvements in the second half and that for 1996 as a whole results should be close to 1995 level.

"In the second half the restarting of the float glass furnace at Czech subsidiary Glavunion, growth in demand and volumes together with the beginning of a recovery in prices and an improvement in the group's financial structure should boost the current result," it said in a statement.
Extraordinary results would be raised by the sale of a 41.76 percent stake in U.S. glass group AFG Industries, resulting in a 1.1 billion franc capital gain.
"However, provisions will have to be increased, in particular to cover the costs of restructuring," it said.
The stake was sold to its majority shareholder Asahi Glass Co Ltd.

Glaverbel said third quarter sales amounted to 8.8 billion francs, down from 9.3 billion francs in the same 1995 period. Adjusted for 1995 acquisitions and divestments, third quarter sales were up 1.6 percent.
Cumulative sales stood at 27.2 billion francs, down four percent from 28.5 billion. Adjusted, sales growth was flat. The contraction was due solely to lower prices since the beginning of 1996.
Volumes since end-June were up on last year's. September and October sales confirmed this trend, it said.
